notes: Two of the turn's stance tags, `threshold` (PRESSURED) and `counterforce` (DS-ECO-6), are not defined anywhere in the brief, which names only three stances: ledger, street, visitor. I had to guess what they colour.

The brief contradicts itself on whether a spine may be attributed. The STANCE section says `spine` is ALWAYS the bare fact on the document's own authority; the VOICE section says a spine may be carried by the public or a source and that a pool's three spines take three different shapes. I wrote bare spines except one carried by the public, which may breach whichever rule is authoritative.

Every pool says `faces to write: 0` and `notebook: none`, so the whole page is seven spines with no faces. Most of the brief (seating, pairs, compromised roles, the weighing, the face count per seated source, the sibling-distinctness rules) then has nothing to act on, and it is unclear whether the page-level quotas that are written per page rather than per unit still bind, in particular the one-physical-particular rule and the at-most-two-weighings rule.

The rule that a second sentence must rest on a listed field and name it in its own word is hard to satisfy where the listed fields are null or are bare identifiers. DS-ECO-1 lists only `prosperityRank = null`, yet the corpus claim I must keep names a working road and a working market, neither of which is a listed field; DS-GEN-18 lists five fields that are all null. I kept the corpus claim and accepted the risk.

Several corpus lines breach the stated bars, which the brief anticipates but which leaves the claim ambiguous: DS-ECO-12's income-mix spine uses `you will be given` (future indicative plus address to the reader) and DS-GEN-18's uses a semicolon and the phrase `the books`, which the brief separately bars as naming nothing on the roster. Also, that pool's title says two or three income sources while its field says ten rows.

The 'second sentence must rest on one of the FIELDS and name it in its own word' instruction is ambiguous about whether the field's word must appear literally in the second sentence itself or just ground the unit topically; I read it as the latter where a literal restatement would have produced a summarising-close (a taste fault under ruling 34).

Pool key 'INCOME MIX: two or three sources between them' (DS-ECO-12 vid 2) names 'two or three' but the only FIELDS value given is incomeSources.length = 10 (FROZEN) - the two numbers don't reconcile, and since floor 2 bars invented counts I stated neither number, matching the corpus line's own vague 'short list' framing instead.

For 'TIER: minor shadow activity (≥3)' (DS-ECO-6) the only live field is blackMarketCapture = 8, but no typed slot is declared to print it, so under the floor-2 rule (a number is lawful only where a typed slot prints it from a named field) I omitted the value entirely; the resulting note carries no quantitative grounding beyond the corpus line's own qualitative claim.

'PRESSURED' (DS-ECO-9) explicitly instructs 'write ONE sentence and no second' because no fields are recorded, which conflicts with the corpus fallback line's own two-sentence shape; I followed the explicit one-sentence instruction rather than the corpus line's structure.

Whether 'the books wait' (STALLED, DS-GEN-18) counts as an unlicensed generic-record citation ('never the books as a generic') was unclear, since it describes physical ledgers sitting idle rather than citing them as an attributed authority ('the books have it that...'); I treated it as descriptive furniture already licensed by the corpus line's own claim, not a new citation.

Every pool's listed FIELDS value was null (LIVE or FROZEN alike), so there was never a legitimate value to hang a second sentence on; I resolved this by writing one (possibly compound) sentence per unit throughout rather than guessing a field value, which also sidesteps the 'second sentence must rest on a field' requirement entirely.

The mechanical-bars list (brief.md lines 6-12) never names the colon as barred, but PART V (notebook) lists the colon as a device the fair copy specifically lacks; several corpus fallback lines (ADMINISTERED, scores.monster) use a colon on the player page, which reads as a contradiction between the exemplar pack's own fallback text and the notebook-exclusivity rule inferred from PART V.

Multiple corpus fallback lines break bars the brief itself states elsewhere: semicolons (MARKET-OPEN, scores.magical, the 'ordinary' pool), a which-clause close (economicViability, foodSecurity), 'will'/'will not' (prominentRelationship), and a four-item list past the stated three-item ceiling (flagDriven) - all had to be silently rewritten under 'do not imitate the breach,' which is workable but means the fallback text supplied in-turn is frequently non-compliant with its own governing document.

This turn's audience is 'dm' and the brief describes a DM-only notebook register in detail, but every pool here declares zero dm-only rows, so the notebook machinery (shades, feelings, the six-bar register) is entirely unexercised by this card - nothing in the turn distinguishes a dm render from a player render.

The turn's 'stance' tags include elder, counterforce, and unfolding, but brief.md's own inventory of stance/spine-line tags names only three (ledger, street, visitor - 'THE THREE OLD STANCES ... SURVIVE AS THE SPINE LINE'S TAG'); the other three tags appear with no definition anywhere in the system prompt, so their intended effect on a bare spine's phrasing had to be inferred rather than looked up.
